headline: KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goyal interacted with the artisan women of Lijjat Papad and commended their women empowerment efforts.
fullText:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goyal interacted with the artisan women of Lijjat Papad and commended their women empowerment efforts.

In line with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Lijjat Papad has emerged as an inspiring example of women empowerment, self-reliance and ‘Local to Global’: KVIC Chairman

30 SEP 2026 10:15PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Manoj Goyal, Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)—under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India—addressed the women artisans of Shri Mahila Griha Udyog Lijjat Papad at an event held on Wednesday at the Sri Shanmukhananda Chandrasekharendra Saraswathi Auditorium in Sion (East), Mumbai. As the chief guest, KVIC Chairman applauded the work of the women artisans and highlighted the significant role played by organizations like Lijjat Papad in advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’.

Addressing the congregation, KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goyal opined that the journey of Lijjat Papad established in 15 March 1959 with just seven women and Rs. 80. It was not merely an initiative to make Papads, but a dream of becoming self-reliant, living with dignity and standing on one's own feet. The recognition of Lijjat Papad as a Village Industry by KVIC in 1966 gave fresh momentum to this journey. Today, through its 83 branches across 16 states, more than 45,000 women are associated with Lijjat Papad and are progressing towards self-reliance and economic independence. Over the years, the organisation has diversified its product range. Besides papads, it also manufactures spices, flour, detergent and liquid soaps. Its products have reached more than 30 countries, including the USA, Australia, Japan and South Africa.

KVIC Chairman Said that the greatest strength of Lijjat Papad is its quality, hard work, and discipline. He remarked that the organization serves as an inspiring example of realizing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Local to Global’. He said, “Lijjat does not merely make papads; it weaves together dignity, self-confidence, and opportunity.”

Shri Goyal said that Lijjat Papad’s achievements have also received national recognition. The organisation was honoured with the Best Village Industry Award in 2003, the Brand Equity Award in 2005 and the Women Development Award in 2017. Several international platforms and media organisations have also showcased Lijjat Papad’s inspiring journey to the world.

Highlighting the activities and initiatives of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), KVIC Chairman said that nearly 5 lakh artisans across the country are being provided employment out of which 80% are women working in around 3,000 Khadi institutions. Over the past 12 years, the wages of Khadi artisans have increased by up to 275 per cent. He further stated that the production of the Khadi and Village Industries sector has increased to approximately ₹1.25 lakh crore, while sales have reached ₹1.87 lakh crore. Under the Village Industry Development Scheme, more than 3.23 lakh machines and toolkits have been distributed during the last 12 years. Similarly, under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), around 11 lakh new projects have been established so far, with subsidies exceeding ₹30,000 crore, generating employment opportunities for approximately 1 crore people.

headline: NBA to Mark 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow with significant progress in Access and Benefit Sharing
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

NBA to Mark 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow with significant progress in Access and Benefit Sharing

Over Rs. 278 Crore realised through ABS; More than Rs. 200 Crore disbursed for Biodiversity Conservation and Community Benefits

30 SEP 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) will mark its 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow, 01.10.2026, with significant progress in translating Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) into tangible outcomes for biodiversity conservation and local communities. Since 2008, the NBA has realised over Rs. 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs. 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and the benefit of communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimants across the country. This progress reflects the strengthening of India’s ABS framework and its ability to connect the use of biological resources with conservation and equitable sharing of benefits. India has emerged as a pioneer in operationalising ABS, supported by a three-tier institutional architecture comprising the NBA at the national level, State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) at the State and Union Territory levels, and Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) at the local level, in accordance with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.

As the NBA marks its 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow, this progress reflects the evolution of ABS into an important instrument for translating the value of biological diversity into conservation action and community benefits. The impact is reflected in a wide network of beneficiaries. The more than Rs. 200 crore disbursed by the NBA has supported over 10,500 BMCs, 28 SBBs, 7 UTBCs, 6 Forest Departments and 58 research institutions and universities across the country for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, research, capacity building and community-oriented activities. Between 01.09.2025 and 31.08.2026, the NBA received Rs. 12.93 crore in ABS amounts and released Rs. 132.01 crore to States, Union Territories, institutions, farmers, local communities and other identified benefit claimants. The releases included accumulated ABS amounts from earlier collections, enabling support for a wider range of conservation and livelihood initiatives.

The ABS mechanism covers a diverse range of biological resources, including agricultural and horticultural crops, plant genetic resources, medicinal and aromatic plants, livestock genetic resources, Red Sanders and microorganisms. Contributions have been received from sectors including seeds, AYUSH, pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, biotechnology, cosmetics, chemicals, biofuels, and food and beverages. Companies such as Nunhems India, East West Seeds India, Pioneer Overseas Corporation, Bayer Bioscience, Himalaya Wellness Company, Dabur India, Organic India, Laurus Labs, Akay Natural Ingredients, Novozymes South Asia, Advanced Enzymes and L’Oréal India, among others, have contributed to the ABS mechanism in accordance with the applicable legal framework.

The benefits are increasingly reaching the ground, supporting the conservation and sustainable use of maize, rice, turmeric, amla, mustard, bitter gourd, cotton, okra and chilli, as well as medicinal and aromatic resources such as kalmegh, elachi, tulsi, guggal gum, neem, garcinia, ashwagandha, pepper and lavanga. Recent releases include Rs. 6.67 crore for 25,431 cotton varieties, Rs. 15.52 crore for mustard-related conservation and Rs. 3.51 crore for 139 okra varieties and 28 hybrids. Around Rs. 100 crore has also been released for the conservation and protection of Red Sanders through the Andhra Pradesh Forest Department and Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board, demonstrating how ABS can translate the value of biological resources into tangible conservation outcomes. At the State and Union Territory levels, over Rs. 51 crore has been generated through ABS approvals granted by SBBs and UTBCs to Section 7 entities (Indian entities) for commercial utilisation of biological resources.

ABS funds are also supporting People’s Biodiversity Registers, habitat restoration, conservation of traditional varieties, medicinal plant conservation, community gene banks, capacity building and sustainable livelihood activities. Where individual benefit claimants cannot be identified, the framework provides for utilisation of funds for the socio-economic development of areas from which biological resources originate. Regulatory reforms and digitalisation have strengthened ease of doing business and ease of compliance, while safeguarding the objectives of biodiversity conservation and fair and equitable benefit sharing. The ABS e-filing system has simplified application processing and improved transparency and tracking. As of now, the NBA has received 11,273 applications, with 6,074 agreements signed/approvals granted and 2,098 certificates issued. Model agreements, standardised procedures and online services have further made the ABS process more predictable and user-friendly. ABS obligations are incorporated into agreements executed by the NBA, providing a clear basis for benefit-sharing payments under the applicable ABS Regulations.

By linking biodiversity conservation with sustainable livelihoods, ABS is contributing to local value addition, sustainable use of biological resources, community participation and livelihood opportunities, particularly in biodiversity-rich rural and tribal areas. It also contributes to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and complements initiatives such as PM-JANMAN, the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Van Dhan, which promote tribal welfare and natural-resource-based livelihoods. India’s ABS framework gives practical effect to the principles of the Nagoya Protocol and advances the country’s commitments under the NBSAP 2024–2030 and the KMGBF, particularly Target 13 on fair and equitable benefit sharing. Through conservation, sustainable use and community benefits, ABS also supports KMGBF Targets 4, 5 and 9 and contributes to relevant SDGs, strengthening the link between biodiversity, livelihoods and sustainable development.

With the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024 and the Biological Diversity (Access and Benefit Sharing) Regulations, 2025, India continues to strengthen a transparent, predictable and effective ABS system, facilitating legitimate access and compliance while ensuring that benefits arising from the utilisation of biological resources contribute to conservation and community well-being. As the NBA marks its 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow, 01.10.2026, it will continue to work with SBBs, UTBCs, BMCs, line departments, research institutions, industry, local communities and other stakeholders to further strengthen ABS implementation. India’s experience demonstrates that ABS can serve as a practical bridge among biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, innovation and community well-being, ensuring that the value generated from India’s biological wealth contributes to its conservation and to the people who sustain it.

(Release ID: 2317351)

headline: Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda Addresses World Congress of Gastroenterology 2026 in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda Addresses World Congress of Gastroenterology 2026 in New Delhi

India Advancing Towards Holistic and Inclusive Healthcare with Greater Emphasis on Prevention and Health Promotion: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda

More Than 600 million Beneficiaries Covered Under AB-PMJAY, Providing ₹5 Lakh Health Cover Per Family: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda

India Recorded 86% Decline in Maternal Mortality Between 1990 and 2023: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda

Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Highlights Government’s Comprehensive Approach to Healthcare at WCOG 2026

30 SEP 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Shri J.P. Nadda, today addressed the World Congress of Gastroenterology (WCOG 2026) in New Delhi. Being held in India for the first time, the four-day international Congress commenced today and will continue till 3 October 2026, bringing together leading experts, clinicians, researchers and healthcare professionals from India and across the world.

With the theme “Transforming Gastrointestinal Health, Preserving Nature,” WCOG 2026 is jointly hosted by the Indian Society of Gastroenterology (ISG) and the World Gastroenterology Organisation (WGO), in collaboration with the Indian National Association for Study of the Liver (INASL), Crohn’s and Colitis Foundation India (CCFI), Indian Pancreas Club (IPC) and Indian Neurogastroenterology and Motility Association (INMA). The Congress focuses on advances in gastrointestinal health through cutting-edge science, clinical practice, research, innovation and multidisciplinary exchange.

Addressing the inaugural session, Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda highlighted the Government’s efforts towards bringing about a comprehensive and holistic approach to healthcare, with greater emphasis on preventive and promotive healthcare alongside curative, rehabilitative and palliative care.

Shri Nadda said that, ‘Under leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the National Health Policy of 2017 marked an important shift towards a comprehensive, holistic and inclusive approach to healthcare, encompassing preventive, promotive, curative and rehabilitative dimensions. Under the policy framework, the Government is strengthening health systems across all levels of care, with emphasis on achieving an optimal balance between primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare and strengthening linkages between different levels of care.

Furthermore, He also highlighted the role of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in strengthening primary healthcare and promoting preventive and promotive health services. He said that the network of around 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs is serving as an important point of contact for people and is helping bring comprehensive primary healthcare closer to communities.

Shri Nadda underlined that screening for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) is an important pillar of preventive healthcare. Through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, population-based screening is being undertaken for people aged 30 years and above for hypertension, diabetes and common cancers, including oral, breast and cervical cancers.

He informed that more than 420 million screenings for hypertension, 420 million for diabetes, 360 million for oral cancer, 170 million for breast cancer and 90 million for cervical cancer have been conducted so far.

The Union Health Minister also highlighted the Government’s efforts to promote healthy dietary practices and active lifestyles. He referred to initiatives such as the Eat Right India campaign of FSSAI and Poshan Maah, which seek to create greater awareness about healthy eating habits and physical activity. He also recalled the Prime Minister’s call to citizens to reduce oil consumption as part of efforts to address obesity and promote healthier lifestyles.

Highlighting the progress made in maternal and child health, Shri Nadda noted that institutional deliveries have increased from 79 per cent in 2015-16 to around 90 per cent, as reflected in the National Family Health Survey. He also referred to improvements in maternal and child health outcomes, noting that between 1990 and 2023, India recorded an 86 per cent decline in maternal mortality, while under-five mortality declined by 79 per cent and neonatal mortality by 70 per cent over the respective period.

Shri Nadda further highlighted the Government’s efforts to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent people, particularly those belonging to economically vulnerable and marginalised sections, from accessing quality healthcare. He said that Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) was launched in September 2018 with the objective of providing financial protection against hospitalisation and ensuring access to necessary healthcare.

Shri Nadda stated that AB-PMJAY provides health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year and has expanded its coverage to more than 600 million beneficiaries, while the scheme has also been extended to around 60 million senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their economic status.

He noted that more than 13 crore treatments have been provided under the scheme, involving healthcare expenditure of over ₹2 lakh crore. He said these achievements reflect the scale of the Government’s efforts to make quality healthcare more accessible to citizens.

He also highlighted measures to improve the affordability of medicines and medical devices. Under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, quality generic medicines are being made available at substantially lower prices compared to branded medicines. He informed that more than 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras are currently serving people across the country and that citizens have collectively saved around ₹45,000 crore on their medicine expenditure through the initiative.

Shri Nadda said that these measures have contributed to reducing the financial burden of healthcare on households. He noted that out-of-pocket expenditure as a proportion of total health expenditure declined from 62 per cent in 2014-15 to 43.4 per cent in 2021-22, reflecting progress towards greater financial protection in healthcare.

He also emphasised that while these achievements provide a strong foundation, continued research and innovation remain essential to address emerging health challenges. He expressed confidence that doctors and researchers working in the field of gastroenterology would contribute innovative solutions to control major gastrointestinal infections and address the evolving burden of gastrointestinal and liver diseases.

Referring to the theme of the Congress, “Transforming Gastrointestinal Health, Preserving Nature,” the Union Health Minister said that the theme is highly relevant in the present context. He expressed confidence that deliberations among leading experts from across the world would contribute to identifying new approaches and solutions for addressing digestive and liver diseases.

Shri Nadda said that international scientific forums such as WCOG provide valuable opportunities for sharing knowledge, learning from different healthcare systems and strengthening international collaboration. He also highlighted the importance of such platforms for young doctors, who would carry forward the next generation of research, clinical practice and innovation in gastroenterology.

Concluding his address, Shri Nadda wished all delegates a successful and productive Congress and invited national and international participants to make full use of the opportunity to exchange knowledge, experiences and ideas during the four-day event.

On the occasion, Shri J.P. Nadda presented Lifetime Achievement Awards to distinguished veterans of the field, recognising their significant contributions to gastroenterology and advancing patient care, research and medical practice.

WCOG 2026 brings together a diverse group of healthcare professionals, including gastroenterologists, hepatologists, pancreatologists, endoscopists, gastrointestinal surgeons, dieticians, nurses, technologists and allied healthcare professionals from across the world. The participation of professionals from different specialties provides an opportunity for exchange of knowledge, experience and best practices.

The Congress also highlights India’s growing contribution to global gastrointestinal research, including in the areas of epidemiology, guidelines and translational medicine. The platform enables Indian and international experts to share research findings, clinical experiences and emerging approaches in gastrointestinal healthcare.

The scientific programme features participation from international and national experts and includes scientific sessions, lectures, debates, workshops, live demonstrations and abstract presentations. The programme also provides opportunities for interaction with industry and technology partners, facilitating discussions on emerging technologies and innovations in gastrointestinal healthcare.

The Congress provides a global platform for knowledge exchange, collaboration and innovation in gastroenterology and allied disciplines. It also offers an opportunity for Indian healthcare professionals, researchers and institutions to engage with the international medical community and contribute to global scientific discussions in the field.

The first-time hosting of the World Congress of Gastroenterology in India marks an important milestone in the country’s engagement with the global gastroenterology community and provides an opportunity to further strengthen international scientific partnerships and multidisciplinary collaboration in healthcare.

Prof. Nikhil Tandon, Director, AIIMS, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India; Dr. Carolina Olano, President, WGO; Dr. Govind Makharia, Chairman, Local Organising Committee (LOC), WCOG; Dr. Mathew Philip, Secretary General, ISG were also present at the Event.

headline: UPSC Centenary Celebrations ‘Manthan’ Focus on Future-Ready Civil Services, Innovation and Constitutional Values
fullText:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

UPSC Centenary Celebrations ‘Manthan’ Focus on Future-Ready Civil Services, Innovation and Constitutional Values

Chairman Dr. Ajay Kumar Reaffirms Commitment to Merit, Fairness and Equal Opportunity as UPSC Completes 100 Years

30 SEP 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) today commenced its two-day centenary celebrations, titled ‘Manthan’, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, marking the completion of 100 years of the institution’s journey. The celebrations brought together senior public functionaries and eminent speakers for deliberations on the evolving role of civil services, innovations in public administration and the institutional values that underpin public service.

Addressing the gathering, UPSC Chairman Dr. Ajay Kumar outlined the Commission’s vision for the next phase of its journey through the three guiding principles of Trust, Transparency and Technology. He emphasised that institutions must adapt to changing circumstances while preserving the principles that are fundamental to their constitutional role.

Dr. Ajay Kumar said that the Commission must change what needs to change so that what must never change can be preserved. While technology and examination formats can evolve, the core constitutional principles of merit, fairness and equal opportunity remain enduring.

The Chairman highlighted the scale and diversity of the Commission’s work, noting that UPSC undertakes approximately 250 distinct recruitment processes every year, covering disciplines ranging from engineering, medical and scientific fields to economics and defence. He also highlighted that the UPSC examination calendar is prepared 18 months in advance, reflecting the extensive planning required for its recruitment processes.

Looking ahead, Dr. Ajay Kumar outlined several initiatives aimed at strengthening the recruitment ecosystem. These include the proposed establishment of a Centre of Excellence to facilitate collaboration and sharing of best practices with State Public Service Commissions. He also referred to the partnership with NALSAR, Hyderabad, for preparation of a compendium of 100 landmark judicial verdicts.

On examination reforms, the Chairman emphasised the importance of assessing candidates for qualities such as reasoning, spontaneous thinking and judgment under ambiguity, rather than their ability to reproduce predictable or coached model answers. He also highlighted the use of digital e-admit cards and face authentication as measures to strengthen examination integrity.

The first session of the centenary deliberations was held on the theme “Role of Civil Services in Viksit Bharat” under the leadership of Smt. Suman Sharma, Member, UPSC. The session brought together Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani, Chief of Defence Staff; Shri Harsh Vardhan Shringla, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and former Foreign Secretary; and Shri Sanjay Shrinet, Chairman, Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission.

Smt. Suman Sharma emphasised the need for outcome-driven administration and highlighted the role of civil servants as primary instruments for translating policy into ground-level outcomes. She called for a shift from procedural excuses towards proactive facilitation and for measuring administration through transformative outcomes on the ground rather than merely through financial expenditure.

Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani highlighted the need to overcome departmental silos, take intelligent risks and demonstrate decisiveness in an environment marked by rapid disruption and increasing civil-military convergence. He underlined the need for an agile and problem-solving civil service.

Shri Harsh Vardhan Shringla emphasised the importance of widening recruitment into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities and aspirational districts, as well as bringing younger candidates into public service. He also referred to the principles of Antyodaya and Nishkama Karma, stressing the responsibility of public servants to serve the last person in the queue.

Shri Sanjay Shrinet emphasised that reforms should empower the grassroots machinery responsible for executing public programmes, noting that the overwhelming majority of the administrative machinery is below Group A level. He called for a shift from authority to accountability and highlighted the importance of administrators functioning as genuine public servants or Sevaks.

Delivering the keynote address at the panel discussion on “Public Service Commissions as a Constitutional Body,” Dr. Ashok Lahiri reflected on the UPSC’s centenary journey and its enduring role in nation-building. He traced the historical evolution of public recruitment from early patronage systems to an impartial constitutional framework rooted in merit, competitive examinations, fairness, and transparency—spanning its milestones from the Public Service Commission in 1926 to the Federal Public Service Commission in 1937, and finally its constitutional status in 1950. Dr. Lahiri underscored the Commission's vital constitutional mandate in upholding equality, justice, and public trust, while highlighting its essential responsibilities beyond recruitment to encompass promotions, service rules, and disciplinary matters

The second session, titled “Innovations in Public Service”, was chaired by Lt Gen Raj Shukla (Retd.), Member, UPSC. Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, delivered the keynote address.

Delivering the keynote address in the second session, Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, commended the UPSC as the “gateway to public service,” lauding its steadfast commitment to integrity, fairness, and perseverance in the selection process. He highlighted key administrative initiatives and innovations introduced by the Government, while outlining a strategic roadmap to advance the vision of Viksit Bharat.

The discussions highlighted the potential of Artificial Intelligence, data analytics and digital architectures to reduce bureaucratic friction and optimise service delivery. The session also emphasised the need for government systems to respond in real time to a confident, aspirational and digitally literate population.

The deliberations further underscored the importance of breaking bureaucratic compartmentalisation, encouraging cross-departmental learning and building a future-ready civil service equipped to respond to emerging challenges.

The centenary discussions also reflected on the Commission’s continuing adoption of technology. UPSC’s technology journey has evolved over several decades, beginning with the introduction of computers in 1978, followed by successive technological interventions in its examination and recruitment processes.

More recent reforms include the introduction of the Universal Registration Number in 2025, randomised interview boards, a dedicated Candidate Helpdesk with a 30-channel IP call centre and a two-level escalation mechanism, and the expansion of examination centres.

In 2026, new examination centres were introduced at Bhubaneswar, Kanpur and Meerut for Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination and at Alwar, Hisar and Kinnaur for NDA & NA (II). The Commission also introduced measures relating to provisional answer keys and the QPRep portal.

The Commission has been strengthening its digital infrastructure and cybersecurity capabilities, while officers are also being trained in emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence. A High-Level Network Committee has been constituted for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity-related requirements.

A significant technological initiative has been the introduction of AI-based facial authentication. Following a pilot at select centres in Gurugram during the NDA & NA (II) and CDS (II) examinations in September 2025, the system was implemented at scale for the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination on 24 May 2026, covering approximately 5.50 lakh candidates. The system uses invigilators’ mobile phones for facial authentication, with the process taking approximately six to eight seconds per candidate.

The centenary also marks a century-long institutional journey that began on 1 October 1926, when the first Public Service Commission in India was constituted as an advisory body. Over the decades, the institution evolved into an independent constitutional body.

The constitutional framework governing Public Service Commissions is contained in Part XIV of the Constitution, under Articles 315 to 323. These provisions establish Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States and provide safeguards relating to the appointment, tenure and removal of their members.

The constitutional framework also provides for the functions of the Commission, including conducting examinations for recruitment to Union services and advising on methods of recruitment, promotions and disciplinary matters. The expenses of the Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund, while the Commission submits an annual report to the President, including cases where its advice has not been accepted.

In carrying out its mandate, UPSC also advises the Government on Recruitment Rules, promotions through Departmental Promotion Committees, induction into the All-India Services and disciplinary cases. During 2023-24, the Commission processed records relating to 24,581 officers for promotion and 532 officers were inducted into the All-India Services.

headline: OPERATION DRISHTI: Armed Forces Medical Services Conduct Two Landmark Mega Eye Surgical Camps in Kashmir
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

OPERATION DRISHTI: Armed Forces Medical Services Conduct Two Landmark Mega Eye Surgical Camps in Kashmir

364 Sight-Restoring Eye Surgeries Performed Across Tangdhar and Srinagar

30 SEP 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

The 11th Mega Eye Surgical Camp under Operation Drishti concluded at 92 Base Hospital, Srinagar, on September 30, 2026, bringing the Kashmir leg of the initiative to a successful close. Across the two mega eye camps conducted at Tangdhar and Srinagar, the surgical team from Army Hospital (Research & Referral) (AHRR), under the leadership of Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, performed 364 eye surgeries, including cataract, glaucoma, pterygium and retinal procedures.

In the weeks preceding the surgical camps, teams from 92 Base Hospital and 328 Field Hospital conducted 18 screening camps across remote and forward areas of the Kashmir Valley, including Tangdhar, Dawar, Machil, Uri, Baramulla, Bandipora, Khanabal and Kangan. Nearly 6,000 people were screened, with around 500 patients identified as requiring surgical intervention. The beneficiaries were subsequently treated in two phases under Operation Drishti.

The first phase was conducted at Tangdhar, in the sensitive sector along the Line of Control (LoC). The camp, held from September 24-25, 2026, marked the first-ever mega eye surgical camp conducted at the LoC in an underground operation theatre. The surgical team successfully performed 220 sight-restoring surgeries over two days, demonstrating the capability to provide advanced ophthalmic care even in remote and operationally challenging locations.

The second phase was conducted at 92 Base Hospital, Srinagar, from September 28-29, 2026, where 144 patients underwent eye surgeries. Several patients with severely impaired vision experienced significant improvement, with some regaining clear vision as early as the following day. In addition to cataract surgeries, the camp provided specialised procedures including glued IOL implantation, glaucoma surgery, pterygium excision and retinal interventions for diabetic retinopathy.

Lieutenant Governor of Jammu & Kashmir, Shri Manoj Sinha, graced the closing ceremony. Addressing the gathering, he appreciated the eye team for its dedication, professional expertise and compassionate service to the people of Kashmir. Lt Gen Balbir Singh, General Officer Commanding, 15 Corps, along with other senior officers, was also present on the occasion.

The initiative brought advanced sub-speciality ophthalmic care closer to people who would otherwise have had to travel long distances for specialised treatment. With the successful completion of its Kashmir leg, Operation Drishti has now reached the North, West, East and Central regions of the country. The next phase of the initiative is scheduled to be conducted in Odisha.

headline: Delhi Records Lowest September Average AQI in Five Years; Air Quality Improvement Trend Continues in 2026

Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Delhi Records Lowest September Average AQI in Five Years; Air Quality Improvement Trend Continues in 2026

30 SEP 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

The improving trend in the overall air quality of Delhi-NCR continues, with Delhi recording its lowest monthly average Air Quality Index (AQI) for September during the current year, as compared to the corresponding period of the last five years, from 2022 to 2026.

The monthly average AQI of Delhi for September during the current year has been recorded at 102, as against 105 in 2025, 105 in 2024, 108 in 2023 and 104 in 2022.

The period from January to September 2026 witnessed the highest number of days with daily average AQI less than 200 (‘Moderate’ category) during the last five years. Delhi recorded 194 such days in 2026, as against 187 days in 2025, 188 days in 2024, 193 days in 2023 and 146 days in 2022.

The period from January to September 2026 also witnessed the lowest number of ‘Poor to Severe+’ days during the last five years, with 79 days in 2026, as against 86 days in 2025, 86 days in 2024, 80 days in 2023 and 127 days in 2022.

The period from January to September 2026 (up to 28.09.2026) has witnessed the joint-lowest average PM2.5 concentration in Delhi compared to the corresponding period since 2022. Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 69 µg/m³ in 2026, as against 69 µg/m³ in 2025, 81 µg/m³ in 2024, 73 µg/m³ in 2023 and 80 µg/m³ in 2022.

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) is working closely with various stakeholders concerned to take effective measures for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution and to improve air quality in Delhi-NCR. These efforts will be further intensified with an endeavour to improve the air quality scenario in Delhi-NCR in the coming days.

Ministry of Minority Affairs observes Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 in New Delhi

Union Minister Shri Kiren Rijiju administers Swachhata Pledge, participates in Shramdaan and tree plantation drive

Shri Rijiju emphasises collective responsibility for cleanliness and highlights ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative

30 SEP 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Minority Affairs observed Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 in New Delhi, today in the presence of Union Minister of Minority Affairs and Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju. The programme included a Swachhata Pledge, Shramdaan and a tree plantation drive.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Rijiju emphasised that cleanliness must be treated as a continuous responsibility rather than a one-time exercise. He said that while existing waste needs to be cleaned, equal emphasis must be placed on creating awareness so that people do not litter in the first place. He further stressed that cleanliness is a collective responsibility and should not be viewed as the responsibility of sanitation workers alone.

“Cleanliness is everyone’s responsibility. It is not enough to speak about cleanliness; it must be brought into our everyday conduct,” the Minister said, while underlining the need to take cleanliness forward in mission mode.

Referring to the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Rijiju noted that the Swachh Bharat Mission has generated widespread awareness regarding cleanliness across the country. He called for sustained public participation to further strengthen the movement and make cleanliness a part of everyday behaviour.

As part of the programme, Shri Rijiju administered the Swachhata Pledge. Participants resolved to remain personally committed to cleanliness, devote time to Shramdaan, begin the effort from their homes, neighbourhoods and workplaces, and encourage others to contribute towards building a cleaner India. The pledge also recalled Mahatma Gandhi’s vision of a clean and developed India.

Linking cleanliness with environmental conservation, the Minister also highlighted the importance of tree plantation and referred to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative. He said that the campaign encourages every individual to plant at least one tree in the name of their mother, thereby connecting environmental responsibility with a deeply respected personal bond.

Shri Rijiju also noted that ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ has gained recognition beyond India. Recalling a recent visit to Europe, he said that during a plantation programme in Belgrade, ministers from other countries told him that they were aware of the campaign being undertaken in India.

The Minister thereafter participated in the Shramdaan and tree plantation drive along with officers and officials of the Ministry.

The occasion also marked the culmination of Hindi Pakhwada observed by the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Addressing the gathering, Shri Rijiju highlighted the importance of Hindi and other Indian languages and emphasised the need to take pride in one’s mother tongue while respecting India’s rich linguistic diversity.

Speaking on the occasion, the Principal of Dyal Singh College highlighted the importance of individual civic behaviour in sustaining cleanliness and called upon citizens to contribute actively to the national resolve for a clean India.

The programme reflected the Ministry of Minority Affairs’ continued commitment towards promoting cleanliness, environmental conservation, civic responsibility and public participation in furtherance of the vision of a Swachh Bharat.

headline: Social Justice & Empowerment Ministry Organizes National Level SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir Under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
fullText:

Social Justice & Empowerment Ministry Organizes National Level SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir Under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign

Shivir Recognises and Honours Contribution of SafaiMitras and Facilitates Access to Health, Safety and Social Protection Measures

Film on NAMASTE Scheme Screened; Swacchta, NMBA Pledges Taken On Spot

30 SEP 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 Campaign, themed Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat, the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment organized the national level SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir in the National Capital here today.

The theme of the Shivir was Samman Safai Mitron Ka, Sankalp Swachh Bharat Ka. The national-level programme was organised in hybrid mode, in which Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) and line departments participated virtually from across the country.

The programme was attended by Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon’ble Chief Minister, NCT of Delhi; Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment; Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice & Empowerment; Shri Pravesh Wahi, Mayor, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD); Shri Sanjeev Khirwar, Commissioner, MCD; Dr Sandeep R. Rathod, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment; Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Managing Director, National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) along with senior officers of the Ministry and officials of MCD, among other dignitaries.

The Shivir at Kedarnath Sahni Auditorium, Dr. S.P.M. Civic Centre, was organized to recognize and honour the contribution of SafaiMitras and sanitation workers and facilitate their access to healthcare, safety, welfare and social protection measures. It provided a single-window platform for sanitation workers and their families to obtain information and assistance regarding various Government schemes and services, while reinforcing the importance of their contribution to public health, cleanliness and the well-being of communities.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon’ble Chief Minister, NCT of Delhi, emphasised that sanitation workers are being provided appropriate safety equipment and that their contribution must be recognised with dignity and respect. She highlighted various initiatives of the Delhi Government for different sections of society, including the Pink Card facility providing free bus travel to women, the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana, 450 Arogya Mandirs for multiple health tests and 611 Palna Kendras for the children of working women.

Smt. Rekha Gupta stressed that maintaining cleanliness is not the sole responsibility of SafaiMitras and sanitation workers but a collective responsibility of every citizen. She called for ensuring that sanitation workers receive their rightful entitlements and emphasised that the safety and dignity of women sanitation workers deserve particular attention. She also highlighted measures to promote mechanisation of sanitation work, including the recent approval of 1,000 litter-picking machines and 100 sweeping machines, aimed at reducing risks associated with manual cleaning activities. She further informed that a top-up health coverage of ₹5 lakh over the existing ₹5 lakh Ayushman Bharat coverage would enhance the total health coverage available to beneficiaries to ₹10 lakh.

Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment, highlighted the Government’s efforts under the NAMASTE Scheme to extend support and welfare measures to Sewer and Septic Tank Workers and Waste Pickers. He emphasised that ensuring the safety and dignity of sanitation workers remains a key priority and that sustained efforts are required to facilitate their integration into the mainstream of society.

Dr. Virendra Kumar underlined that NAMASTE goes beyond welfare assistance by focusing on the safety, dignity and long-term social and economic inclusion of sanitation workers. He highlighted the extension of benefits to Sewer and Septic Tank Workers and Waste Pickers and stressed the importance of ensuring that eligible workers are connected with healthcare, social security and safety-related interventions. He emphasised that sanitation workers should be enabled to lead lives with dignity and become an integral part of the mainstream of society.

Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice & Empowerment, highlighted the Government’s sustained focus on sanitation and the welfare of sanitation workers since 2014. He noted that the scope of the NAMASTE Scheme has been extended to workers associated with Fecal Sludge Treatment Plants (FSTPs) and Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs), along with benefits such as Ayushman Cards and PPE kits.

Shri B. L. Verma emphasised that access to welfare benefits must be accompanied by adherence to prescribed safety guidelines and protocols. He also underlined the importance of citizen participation and responsible behaviour towards sanitation workers, reiterating that cleanliness and the dignity of persons engaged in sanitation work are a shared responsibility.

Shri Pravesh Wahi, Mayor, MCD, highlighted the importance of safeguarding the rights and welfare of sanitation workers. He informed that more than 3,000 SafaiMitras had been formalised in the MCD and emphasised the provision of appropriate safety equipment, including PPE kits, to enable sanitation workers to perform their duties safely.

Shri Sanjeev Khirwar, Commissioner, MCD, acknowledged the efforts of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and MCD towards strengthening sanitation work and improving support for sanitation workers. He also appreciated the contribution of NSKFDC in facilitating welfare and support measures for sanitation workers.

The Shivir also provided an opportunity for sanitation workers and their dependents to access a range of health, safety and social protection services. Preventive health check-ups and screening services were facilitated for SafaiMitras and their dependents, while PPE kits and other safety equipment were distributed and demonstrated. Eligible sanitation workers and their families were facilitated in accessing Central and State Government welfare and social protection schemes. The programme provided information and facilitation relating to schemes and services such as Ayushman Bharat/PM-JAY, PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Swachhata Udyami Yojana and PM Jan Dhan Yojana, subject to eligibility. Assistance was also provided regarding eligibility criteria, application procedures and registration processes for various welfare and social protection schemes.

Parallel programmes were also organised by Urban Local Bodies across the country. These programmes featured live webcasting of the national-level event and included activities aimed at promoting the dignity, safety, health and welfare of sanitation workers. Eligible SafaiMitras, sanitation workers and waste pickers were facilitated in accessing relevant benefits and services, including PPE kits, Ayushman Cards and other welfare and social protection measures.

The gathering also took the Swachhata Pledge, reaffirming a collective commitment towards cleanliness, hygiene and responsible civic participation. The pledge reinforced the spirit of “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag” and encouraged citizens to contribute towards creating a cleaner and healthier India.

Besides, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan pledge was also administered in which the gathering participated reaffirming their commitment to Drug Free Society-Drug Free India.

A film on NAMASTE Scheme was screened on the occasion.

On the occasion, the Ayushman Cards with upto Rs 5 Lakh healthcare coverage, were distributed among the SafaiMitras.

The SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to placing the health, safety, dignity and social security of sanitation workers at the centre of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign. The programme highlighted the vital contribution of SafaiMitras and sanitation workers to public health, cleanliness and the quality of life of communities across the country.

On this occasion, the experts demonstrated the safety drill while sporting PPE kits and other safety gear.

The nationwide observance provided an opportunity to recognize and appreciate SafaiMitras and sanitation workers for their essential contribution and to strengthen collective efforts towards ensuring their safety, dignity, welfare and social security. It reinforced the message that the vision of a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat can be achieved through the active participation, protection and recognition of every individual contributing to sanitation and cleanliness.

headline: Union Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav launches Guidelines for National Coastal Mission 2.0
fullText:

Union Environment Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav launches Guidelines for National Coastal Mission 2.0

₹767 crore Central Sector Scheme to be implemented till 2030-31 across nine coastal States and four Union Territories

30 SEP 2026 7:31PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today launched the Guidelines for implementation of National Coastal Mission (NCM 2.0), in New Delhi.

This Central Sector Scheme, with an approved outlay of ₹767 crore, would be implemented till 2030-31 across nine coastal States and four Union Territories of the country. The scheme aims at strengthening the resilience and sustainability of India’s coastal regions and unlocking the potential of Blue economy. It would be implemented through active participation and collaboration with coastal States/ UTs and stakeholders.

While launching the Guidelines, Shri Yadav highlighted that the Mission will strengthen coastal resilience through vulnerability assessments, ecosystem restoration, pollution management, biodiversity conservation, sustainable tourism, spatial planning, research and capacity building. It would further promote ease of doing business through a clear and streamlined implementation framework.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has always highlighted that the Blue Chakra in the Indian National Flag symbolizes the immense potential of India’s Blue Economy. Guided by his vision, NCM 2.0 will drive towards the sustainable development of the country’s coastal regions, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

The Guidelines provide a clear and enabling framework for the effective, transparent and timely implementation of NCM 2.0, ensuring convergence with ongoing government schemes. By promoting a whole-of-government approach, streamlining processes, clarifying institutional responsibilities, and strengthening monitoring and accountability, the Guidelines will facilitate coordinated implementation between the Central and State government

headline: Scientific Steering Committee on One Health Reviews Progress Towards Strengthening One Health Systems in India
fullText:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI

Scientific Steering Committee on One Health Reviews Progress Towards Strengthening One Health Systems in India

30 SEP 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Sixth Meeting of the Scientific Steering Committee on One Health was held on 30 September 2026 at Kartavya Bhavan 3, New Delhi under the chairmanship of Prof. Ajay K. Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India.

At the outset, substantial progress made in operationalising the One Health approach beyond its initial convergence framework was noted. Prof. Sood underscored the importance of clear institutional ownership, outcome‑oriented targets, and consistent follow-through to ensure that the Committee’s recommendations translate into action on the ground. He also highlighted the value of building on ongoing programmes, established platforms, and current institutional capacities rather than creating parallel structures. Prof. Sood noted that such alignment would improve information flow, support coordinated decision‑making, and enable timely action across human, animal, and environmental health domains.

The Minimum Standard Requirements (MSR) document for BSL-3/4 laboratories developed by the Advisory and Review Committee on BSL 3/4 laboratories was released during the meeting. The document will shortly be made available in the public domain for wider dissemination and reference.

The Committee reviewed progress towards developing an interoperable One Health Dashboard and deliberated on areas requiring continued inter-sectoral coordination. The Committee also appreciated efforts made by MoH&FW towards the next phase of the Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) and noted that there are potential complementarities between IHIP and the proposed One Health Dashboard. Members discussed opportunities to strengthen existing systems and mechanisms and advance the implementation of One Health priorities at the national and sub-national levels.

In his concluding remarks, Prof. Sood commended the progress made in developing an interoperable One Health Dashboard. He urged Ministries and Departments to sustain collaborative engagement, strengthen follow‑up processes, and identify areas where greater convergence and support could accelerate implementation. He emphasised that an interoperable One Health Dashboard reflects not only a whole‑of‑government effort but a whole‑of‑country approach providing integrated visibility across sectors and ensuring that health threats are addressed holistically rather than in isolation.

The meeting reaffirmed the Government of India’s commitment to advancing an integrated One Health approach and strengthening national preparedness through coordinated, cross‑sectoral action.

The meeting was attended by Dr Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of PSA (OPSA) and secretaries of stakeholder ministries/department which included Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health (DHR) and Director General (DG) Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR); Prof Umesh Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST); Dr Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General (DG), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR); Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush; Dr V. Narayana, Chairman, Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO); and Dr Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). Participants also included Dr Rakesh Gupta, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW); Dr Naveena B. Maheswarappa, Animal Husbandry Commissioner, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) and other Senior representatives from ICMR; Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEF&CC); Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) & Security Services; DAHD; ICAR; Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Ayush; National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC); Department of Fisheries; National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), National Institute for One Health (NIOH); OPSA and Gujarat state representatives. Additionally, the meeting was joined by the chairs of the Advisory and Review Committees viz. Lt. Gen. (Rtd.) Dr Madhuri Kanitkar (BSL-3/4 laboratory network), Dr N.K. Arora (technology-enabled surveillance), and Dr Vijay Chandru (data integration and data sharing) and members of Technical Working Group for One Health Dashboard.

headline: District Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan as part of Shram Samvad Initiative
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

District Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan as part of Shram Samvad Initiative

30 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment, in collaboration with FICCI and the Bhiwadi Manufacturers Association, organised the “Shram Samvad” District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes at BMA House, Industrial Area, Bhiwadi, Rajasthan today. The programme aimed to build awareness among employers and industry stakeholders about the Labour Codes, which came into force on 21st November 2025, and the Central Rules, notified on 08th May 2026, while highlighting the key provisions and compliance requirements under the new framework. The programme brought together more than 100 participants from diverse sectors, including employers, industry representatives, HR professionals, legal experts, finance specialists, and other key stakeholders in the labour and employment ecosystem.

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the Government of India.

The inaugural address was delivered by Shri Yogesh Jain, General Secretary, Bhiwadi Manufacturers Association (BMA). This was followed by a keynote address by Shri Ashutosh A.T. Pednekar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, who highlighted the key provisions of the Labour Codes and the Ministry’s vision for organising the ‘District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programmes’ across the country.

The first technical session was conducted by Shri Om Prakash Singh, Labour Welfare Commissioner (Central), who presented a comprehensive overview of the Labour Codes, their objectives, and the major reforms introduced through the new legislative framework. The session helped participants understand the broader vision and significance of labour law reforms for both employers and workers.

The second session, conducted jointly by Shri Nitesh Bhasin, Under Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, and Shri Om Prakash Singh, Labour Welfare Commissioner (Central), focused on the key compliance requirements for employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new framework.

A Q&A session was conducted as part of the event, that encouraged active participation and engagement from attendees. Participants shared their perspectives, highlighted field-level challenges, and raised queries relating to labour welfare, employer obligations, and social security provisions, setting the stage for the subsequent technical sessions and deliberations.

The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was led by Shri Bhupendra Yadav, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). Participants were briefed on the scheme’s objectives, eligibility conditions, and benefits aimed at promoting employment generation.

The fourth session covered the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Shri Pravin P. Mohandas, Welfare Commissioner (Central), Ajmer. The session highlighted the scheme’s key features and its role in extending pension and social security benefits to workers in the unorganised sector.

The programme concluded with a second interactive question-and-answer session, during which participants engaged directly with the speakers and sought clarifications on various aspects of the Labour Codes, employer compliance, and social security schemes.

The vote of thanks was delivered by Shri Surendra Singh Chauhan, Member, FICCI Rajasthan State Council, and Past President, BMA. He urged the authorities to continue supporting initiatives that would further strengthen Bhiwadi’s position as one of the country's leading industrial hubs.

The event served as a key platform for capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and awareness generation, fostering a deeper understanding of the Labour Codes and supporting their effective implementation through informed participation by employers and industry stakeholders.

headline: Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy to Participate in Cleanliness Drive under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Mines

Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy to Participate in Cleanliness Drive under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

Ministry of Mines to Undertake Cleanliness and Beautification Initiatives and Launch One-Month E-Waste Collection Drive

30 SEP 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, will participate in the “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” collective voluntary Shramdaan being organised by the Ministry of Mines under the Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign at Yashwant Place, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, on October 1, 2026. During the programme, the Union Minister will join officers, employees and sanitation workers in cleanliness activities and interact with the personnel engaged in maintaining the public space. The one-hour collective Shramdaan will bring together participants in a shared effort towards cleanliness and upkeep of the surrounding areas, reinforcing the spirit of Jan Bhagidari, dignity of work and collective responsibility for a cleaner and greener environment.

As part of the Ministry’s wider Swachhata Hi Seva initiatives, the Ministry of Mines has adopted a park at GPOA-3, Netaji Nagar, New Delhi, for planned landscaping, beautification and improvement of the surrounding area. The initiative will focus on developing the identified space into a cleaner, greener and well-maintained public area, while promoting sustainable practices and greater ownership of shared spaces.

The Union Minister will also inaugurate an E-Waste Collection Stall at GPOA-3, marking another important initiative under SHS 2026. The stall will facilitate the collection of discarded electronic and electrical items and encourage officials and employees to adopt responsible practices for disposal of e-waste. The initiative will also create awareness about the importance of segregation, collection and authorised recycling of e-waste.

The E-Waste Collection Drive will be conducted for one month from October 2 to October 31, 2026. During this period, officials and employees will be encouraged to bring their discarded electronic items to the designated collection point. The collected e-waste will be channelised for appropriate recycling and scientific processing through authorised mechanisms.

A key focus of the initiative will be to highlight the resource value of e-waste, particularly its potential for recovery of critical minerals and other valuable materials. Electronic and electrical products contain a range of materials that can be recovered through appropriate recycling and processing. Their recovery can contribute to resource efficiency, reduce dependence on virgin materials and support the principles of a circular economy.

The initiative is in line with the Ministry of Mines’ broader efforts to promote responsible resource utilisation, circular economy practices and recovery of critical minerals from secondary sources. By linking cleanliness with responsible e-waste management and resource recovery, the campaign will encourage sustainable practices in everyday life.

The Ministry of Mines continues to undertake various activities under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, with emphasis on cleanliness, sanitation, waste management, environmental sustainability and citizen participation. The initiatives at Yashwant Place and GPOA-3 will reinforce the Ministry’s commitment to making Swachhata a sustained collective effort and promoting a cleaner, greener and more resource-efficient future.

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Organises Shramdaan under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’

Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary Department of Health Research Leads Cleanliness Drive; Senior Officials and Staff Participate with Enthusiasm

Ministry Emphasises Jan Bhagidari, Collective Responsibility and the Linkage between Cleanliness and Public Health

01 OCT 2026 10:08AM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare organised a voluntary cleanliness drive (shramdaan) under the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ campaign near Gate No. 3 of Kartavya Bhavan-1, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Marg, New Delhi, today.

Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), led the shramdaan. Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Health Mission (NHM); Dr. Rakesh Gupta, Additional Secretary and Director General, National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO); Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS); and other senior officials and staff of the Ministry participated in the cleanliness drive.

The officials and staff participated with enthusiasm and dedication, reaffirming the spirit of collective action embodied in the campaign theme, ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’.

Speaking to the media on the occasion, Dr. Rajiv Bahl highlighted the importance of making cleanliness a sustained collective effort and encouraged officials and citizens to contribute actively towards maintaining clean and healthy surroundings.

Smt. Aradhana Patnaik emphasised the importance of Jan Bhagidari and individual responsibility in promoting cleanliness and creating healthier public spaces. She highlighted that sustained cleanliness requires active participation and responsible action by every individual.

The cleanliness drive formed part of the ongoing ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ campaign, which seeks to strengthen Jan Bhagidari and encourage citizens to actively contribute towards cleanliness efforts across the country. The campaign underscores that lasting cleanliness is not only an institutional responsibility but also a shared societal commitment requiring sustained public participation and collective action at the community level.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reiterated its commitment to the objectives of Swachh Bharat and highlighted the close linkage between cleanliness, public health and healthy living. The Ministry emphasised that sustained awareness, responsible waste management and active citizen participation are essential for creating cleaner, healthier and more sustainable public spaces.
